text:
sarah_support: escalation from a customer running our Python SDK in CI — they can install fine locally but CI build fails on import. They attached a minimal repro and error.

sarah_support: repro (Dockerfile):
```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-alpine3.17
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml .
RUN pip install -U pip setuptools
RUN pip install .[async]  # installs redwood-sdk with extras
COPY . .
CMD ["python", "-c", "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"]
```

sarah_support: error from CI when running the container:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
    from .async_client import AsyncClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood.async_client' (/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py)
```

sarah_support: pip freeze inside CI shows: `httpx==0.15.8`, `redwood-sdk==1.4.0`

sarah_support: customer says they have a constraints.txt in their org that pins httpx to 0.15 for an older internal dependency. they can't easily change it. Any ideas for a workaround?

mike_devex: thanks for the details — that ImportError reads like a mismatch where our package is importing AsyncClient from httpx / our wrapper but CI ended up with an old httpx that doesn't expose the same API. redwood-sdk's async extra requires httpx>=0.23 (we updated last year).

mike_devex: two quick options: ask customer to override the constraint (hard), or install our package without extras and vendor the needed HTTP transport separately so httpx isn't pulled in via extras. e.g.:
```bash
# install sdk core without deps, then force compatible httpx
pip install --no-deps redwood-sdk==1.4.0
pip install 'httpx>=0.23.0'
# then install other deps they need that depend on older httpx in a separate env or namespace
```

julia_eng: adding context — in pyproject.toml we have: 
```toml
[project.dependencies]
# core deps omitted

[project.optional-dependencies]
async = ["httpx>=0.23", "anyio>=3"]
```

julia_eng: that confirms our extras require newer httpx. The ImportError stack points to our internal `redwood.async_client` expecting httpx.AsyncClient shape.

ben_support: customer says they can't split envs and constraints.txt is applied by their global CI policy. they asked if we can support older httpx 0.15 as a temporary compatibility shim.

mike_devex: supporting 0.15 would be heavy — a lot changed. But we could provide a small compatibility module they can install into their app that wraps the older API. Two approaches:
- publish a tiny package `redwood-httpx-compat` that detects older httpx and provides the missing symbols (ugly).
- or provide a known-good wheel they can vendor into CI (copy the wheel into the image) so our expected httpx version is present but doesn't rely on pip network access.

mike_devex: example of vendoring a wheel in Docker: 
```dockerfile
# build stage or ci cache has httpx-0.23.3.whl and redwood-sdk-1.4.0.whl
FROM python:3.11-alpine3.17
WORKDIR /app
COPY wheels/httpx-0.23.3-py3-none-any.whl /tmp/
COPY wheels/redwood_sdk-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl /tmp/
RUN pip install /tmp/httpx-0.23.3-py3-none-any.whl /tmp/redwood_sdk-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

sarah_support: customer asked if a `pip install --no-deps` + manual httpx would break anything else in our SDK (like TLS backends on Alpine).

julia_eng: on Alpine you need `openssl` and musl-related wheels. If they use pure-Python httpx wheel it should be fine but they must ensure `cffi`/`cryptography` are available. Suggest they use manylinux wheel on non-alpine or use `python:3.11-slim` instead of alpine to avoid musl pain.

ben_support: customer says switching base image is possible but their org forbids non-alpine images due to size policy. they'd prefer a small patch from us.

mike_devex: OK, I'll draft a tiny compatibility shim we can drop in as a short-term stopgap and share as a gist. But also recommend filing a support ticket to get an exception for pinning older httpx — it's brittle long-term.

ops-bot: created support ticket #4521 and linked to this thread.

sarah_support: perfect — please drop the gist/patch here and I'll forward to the customer. Also logging the workaround steps in the ticket. :thumbsup:

mike_devex: posted gist with compatibility shim code and instructions (link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/devex/httpx-compat). gist includes: detection of httpx import, small wrapper exposing `AsyncClient` and thin adapter for `request` signatures. notes it is not intended for production, just an unblock for CI.

ben_support: customer accepted the wheel-vendoring approach for now. closing loop after I confirm they can run their CI image with the vendored wheel.

sarah_support: thanks everyone. I'll mark the ticket as triaged and will follow up if they hit cryptography/build issues in Alpine.
